decisionRationale: Phases 2, 5, 6, 7 and 9 were not executed: Electron lifecycle/security, document ingestion, Quartz/source routing, import/export and UX abuse/races.
A clean worktree at HEAD fails 123 dashboard tests, and SH1 repair worktrees are cut from HEAD, so repairs currently verify against that baseline.
The Week 1 intermittent scenarios are not root-caused; the upload/backdrop case did not reproduce in 10 controlled attempts, which is evidence against a persistent defect but not an explanation.

revision.workingTree: dirty and preserved; 134+ uncommitted entries, actively edited by the developer during this session
revision.note: A clean-worktree run at this same revision produced 123 dashboard failures versus 51 in the working tree, so the uncommitted work is net-fixing. Repair worktrees are cut from HEAD and therefore start from the larger failure set.

B-2.mechanism: The gate is now the issuer of the only supported writer. applyGatedMutation is the sole write path, and finalizeRepairCapability compares the worktree diff against the files the capability actually wrote, so any ungated edit is detected and the repair cannot be certified.
enforcedInvariants: no root cause or responsible code path => no capability
finding revision != worktree HEAD => no capability (stale replay)
forbidden trust boundary in allowedPaths => no capability
existing QA oracle declared as the regression test => no capability
write to a forbidden path => denied
write to an existing QA oracle with a product capability => denied
path traversal out of the worktree => denied
reuse after finalize, after revoke, or after expiry => denied
unauthorised worktree change at finalize => repair cannot be certified
receipt validation requires a finalized capability whose findingId matches
B-2.residualLimitation: A correctness boundary inside the QA controller, not an OS sandbox. It does not stop an arbitrary process from editing files; it makes an ungated edit impossible to certify as a repair.
